environment.description: Same Django REST API on AWS ECS Fargate with Amazon RDS PostgreSQL 14. Database connection uses 'app_tenant_user' role. PostgreSQL has ALTER TABLE documents ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY with policy: CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON documents USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant')::uuid) WITH CHECK (tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant')::uuid). The role app_tenant_user is NOT a table owner and does not have BYPASSRLS privilege. Additionally, a pg_hba.conf entry restricts this role to connections only from the ECS task subnet CIDR. The ALB has a Lambda@Edge authorizer that validates X-Tenant-ID against the JWT sub claim from Cognito token - mismatched tenant headers receive 403 before reaching the application. Note: the in-memory cache bypass is still present in code but the Lambda@Edge ensures a tenant can only ever issue requests with their own verified tenant_id, and RLS ensures the DB never returns rows from other tenants regardless of the SET command value.

config.database: PostgreSQL 14, RDS, RLS FORCE enabled on documents table
config.rls_policy: CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON documents FOR ALL USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant')::uuid) WITH CHECK (tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant')::uuid)
config.db_user_permissions: GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON documents TO app_tenant_user (no BYPASSRLS, not table owner)
config.force_rls: ALTER TABLE documents FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY
config.infrastructure: ECS Fargate, ALB with Lambda@Edge authorizer
config.header_validation: Lambda@Edge validates X-Tenant-ID matches JWT sub claim from Cognito; rejects mismatches with 403
